references.text: Jesus' teaching in the temple with great openness (parrēsia) toward the people, despite his lack of formal education, creates the same wonder among the leaders as in 7:26.
The people's direct question about whether Jesus is the Messiah, and their doubt based on knowing his background, mirrors the leaders' speculation in 7:26 about whether they have recognized him.
The chief priests and Pharisees gather to discuss Jesus' actions and fear that the whole nation will believe in him, reflecting the leaders' concern in 7:26 that 'the rulers' have recognized him.
The Pharisees admit they have accomplished nothing because the whole world is running after Jesus, confirming the fear expressed in 7:26 that the leaders have actually recognized him as the Messiah.
The high priest asks Jesus directly about his teaching and disciples, and Jesus answers with openness (parrēsia) that he has spoken openly to the world, linking back to the observation in 7:26.
